W1–W3 retain the agreed project labels. They are not verification of FBMP automatic wind/uplift pairing or automatic combination settings.
DC / PL / W1–W3 — NODE ENTRY TABLE
Forces are in kip. Moments use the selected entry units. Positive components act along the displayed positive axes; physical upward wind is retained when V is reversed.

Moment units:
kip-ft
Enter DC and PL once as separate load cases. The W rows contain wind only, including the matching residual node moments. Do not add DC or PL to each W row.
DC = superstructure dead load at the pad; PL = pedestrian live load. Neither includes the other. Cap/pier-wall self-weight is excluded from these entries because the source assumes FBMP supplies it.
Cheek-wall/pedestal dead weight and direct cap/wall wind are not in this node-entry table. They are listed separately on the next page to avoid duplication.
For the opposite wind directions, change the controls and use the recalculated complete sets. Do not multiply an uplift set by -1: deck uplift must remain upward.
Use the displayed residual moments at the displayed node elevation. Do not also apply the original elevated resultants, per-bearing breakdown components, or C004 two-node condensed moments.
OTHER APPLICATIONS / COMBINATION REFERENCE
DIRECT CAP / PIER WIND — SEPARATE FROM B1–B4

Apply the total to the actual exposed-face centroid or equivalent wall/cap nodes—not once to the cap and again to the wall. The source does not establish those coordinates; transferred direct-wind moments remain unresolved. W1/W3 also require direction-consistent direct-pier cases.
ADDITIONAL GRAVITY — NOT INCLUDED IN THE MASTER DC ROWS
Both columns are signed V-entry forces in the displayed axis system. Below-pad DC is the lumped cheek-wall/pedestal weight: use actual local weights or equivalent shares once. DW is a separate case.
SOURCE COMBINATION FACTORS — APPLY AFTER CASE ENTRY

This is the source DC/DW/PL/wind subset, not all project actions. Evaluate applicable maximum/minimum permanent-load patterns and required wind directions. Do not factor an already combined source vertical-load result again.
ENTRY-TRANSFORMATION CHECKS — NOT MEMBER CAPACITY

The checks compare mapped entry resultants with the original source resultants, including coordinate handedness. They do not verify the actual .in file, automatic combinations, restraints, or structural resistance.

section.heading: Wind components and equivalent cap-node actions
section.paragraph: C002 supplies the simplified horizontal cases. C001 and C004 supply the perpendicular horizontal-plus-uplift cases. Each case below is separate; do not add a simplified case to an uplift case. The prescribed fence pressure remains unchanged between limit states. Horizontal shear sharing is equal between the two beam lines within each span and proportional to the separate span tributaries, retaining the source load-path assumption.

The remaining roll couple at each cap node is the transverse force times the distance from the node elevation to the bearing plane. Longitudinal source moments are retained as equivalent cap-node pitch couples; they are not individual elastomeric-pad moment demands. A verified restraint model is needed to resolve that longitudinal action into physical pad forces.

section.heading: Load factors and combined vertical node loads
section.paragraph: Basis: LRFD Tables 3.4.1-1 and 3.4.1-2, 10th Edition (2024). Maximum/minimum permanent-load factors apply according to whether the force effect increases or reduces the demand. The rows are a gravity/wind subset; mixed stabilizing and destabilizing permanent-load patterns may also govern.
GRAVITY/WIND SUBSET OF THE MODEL COMBINATIONS

These combinations collect the displayed DC, DW, pedestrian and structure-wind actions only. Other applicable project actions remain separate. Do not scale the Strength III wind set to obtain Service I: concrete and fence components have different limit-state treatment.
COMBINED CAP-NODE VERTICAL ACTION — SELECTED WIND SIGNS

For manual application of a combined row, use F_V = −N and the matching wind force/couple tables. Do not factor these combined values again. When using FBMP load-combination factors, enter the separate unfactored gravity and matching wind cases instead.
section.heading: Direct wind on the pier — separate application
section.paragraph: Direct cap/wall wind does not pass through the bearings and is not included in B1–B4. The following face-normal forces are source-model component bounds, not one simultaneous full-force pair. The simplified case requires direction-consistent direct-pier loads; the 25% superstructure rule is not a direction-angle definition for the wall.
DIRECT-PIER WIND BOUNDS — KIP

For the perpendicular III-U case, pair the signed T direct-pier force with that case, applied at the exposed-face centroid. The idealized L face is parallel to that wind. Actual face-centroid elevations and model wall nodes are not documented by the current four-bearing geometry; complete that separate wall-node mapping before final model loading.
